subject: Indemnity: remediation access vs. notice routing (source-code ask)
messages:
From: Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@apexbio.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@apexbio.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: indemnity + technical remediation access

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Apex is optimistic about Redwood. Legal reviewed the MSA and came back with two key sticking points for us to resolve before procurement signs off:

1) Indemnity carveouts for third-party IP claims (they want broader protection and a lower threshold for notice).
2) A request that, in the event of a third-party IP claim alleging output-generated infringement, Redwood must provide temporary limited source-code access to Apex's designated counsel/engineers to assist with remediation and forensic analysis, under NDA.

We understand this is a sensitive ask. Can you confirm Redwood's general stance on source-code provisioning for customers in remediation scenarios, and who from your side we should loop in for the legal redlines?

Attached are the redlined MSA (annotated by our counsel) and an evidence checklist showing what Apex expects when a claim is raised.

Goal: get to a mutual action plan this week if possible.

Thanks,
Sara Lincoln
Head of Product Ops (Apex Bio)

Attachments: redlined_MSA_v3.pdf, evidence_checklist.xlsx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@apexbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: indemnity + technical remediation access

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redlines. I appreciate how specific Apex's counsel was; that helps.

High level from Redwood: we are comfortable with a robust indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to our product defects, but we have hard limits around: (a) exposure caps, (b) rights we need to retain for defense control, and (c) any permanent requirement to hand over source code.

About the source-code provisioning ask:
- We do not provide general or permanent source-code access.
- For remediation/forensic purposes, we're open to a time-boxed, heavily-scoped engagement where we grant read-only access to a sanitized subset of code/components under a direct vendor-to-counsel NDA and with strict technical controls (audit logs, time-limited credentials, no production write access).
- That scope needs to be narrowly defined in the MSA (what components, what triggers, who can request).

Ben (cc) is leading the evidence/evidence-handling playbook — Ben, can you outline operational controls we can offer (audit log retention, ephemeral access, redaction process)? Marissa — legal please advise on redline language that preserves our defense control while offering the remediation path Sara requests.

Proposed next step: Redwood legal will send a short-term compromise clause that:
1) Limits access to a specified remediation window (e.g., 30 days unless extended by mutual written consent),
2) Requires Apex to provide a prima-facie claim showing (basic evidence) before access is triggered,
3) Limits use of any information obtained to remediation and dispute resolution, and
4) Keeps defense control with Redwood unless Redwood elects otherwise.

If Apex agrees in principle, we can bake a narrow definition into the Order Form and keep the MSA indemnity mechanics (notice, mitigation, defense) consistent.

-Tessa
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 16, 2025 at 09:45 AM Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@apexbio.com> wrote:
> Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll review the proposed compromise.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: technical guardrails for remediation access (draft)

Tessa / Marissa — drafting operational controls as promised. Key items we can offer and should include in the redline:

- Trigger: access only after Apex provides a written notice plus evidence packet showing the alleged infringement (hashes, sample outputs, timestamps).
- Scope: read-only access to the minimal service components that produced the output (in most cases this will be inference logs, chat transcripts, model and prompt metadata, and a sanitized diff of any custom prompt templates). No access to core model weights.
- Timebox: initial 21-day access window; extensions only by mutual written agreement.
- Access mechanism: ephemeral credential tied to a named counsel/engineer, MFA enforced, IP whitelisting, and session recording.
- Data handling: anything copied out requires redaction; derived remediation artifacts remain subject to Redwood's confidentiality; Apex may not rehost Redwood code.
- Escalation: if forensic analysis suggests code-level issues that necessitate further access, both parties must agree on a controlled escalation and a narrowly-scoped escrow-style review with a neutral third-party expert.

I'll attach a one-paragraph operational summary for legal to convert into contract wording. This keeps us from making a blanket commitment to provide source code while demonstrating good-faith remediation support.

--Ben
Director, Customer Security and Ops

Attachment: remediation_controls_onepager.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@apexbio.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: indemnity + technical remediation access

Sara — copied in a short redline excerpt below and a suggested Order Form paragraph that we hope addresses Apex's procurement requirement while protecting Redwood. If Apex is comfortable in principle, I'll upload a marked MSA and an Order Form addendum for signature.

--- Proposed contract language (excerpt) ---
Remediation Access:
"In the event Customer provides written notice meeting the requirements of Section X (Notice of Claim) together with a preliminary evidence packet reasonably demonstrating that Customer has received output from the Service that is the subject of a third party intellectual property claim, Provider (Redwood) shall, at Provider's sole election, make available limited, time-boxed, and auditable technical access to a narrowly-defined subset of Provider's service components for the sole purpose of performing remediation and forensic analysis. Such access shall be: (a) read-only unless otherwise agreed in writing; (b) strictly limited in scope and duration as set forth in an access statement executed by both parties; (c) subject to a tailored protective order or NDA; and (d) not constitute a waiver of Provider's right to control the defense of the Claim. The parties agree to use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize exposure to Provider's proprietary source code and to rely first on logs, metadata, and derivative artifacts for analysis."

We also propose adding an Order Form addendum that lists the operational controls Ben outlined (trigger evidence, 21-day window, session recording, escalation path to neutral third-party).

If Apex confirms the addendum approach is acceptable, procurement can get a narrow, signature-ready package instead of reopening every MSA clause.

Sara — can you confirm whether Apex's counsel will accept an Order Form-level addendum (operational) plus the narrow MSA excerpt above? If so, we'll prepare final redlines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Legal — Contracts
